Q: Filter by group value A:

A window function might be fastest

WITH cte AS (
    SELECT *,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE yt.STATUS = 'error')
        OVER (PARTITION BY yt.ID) AS count_error
    FROM yourTable yt
)
SELECT
  cte.ID,
  cte.STATUS
FROM cte
WHERE cte.count_error = 0;

Q: Fail vs. raise in Ruby : Should we really believe the style guide? A:

use 'raise' for exceptions to be caught, and 'fail' for serious errors which are not meant to be handled

This is not what the Rubocop style guide or the link you provided say on the matter.

What is meant here is use raise only in rescue blocks. Aka use fail when you want to say something is failing and use raise when rethrowing an exception.

As for the "does it matter" part - it is not one of the most hardcore strictly followed rules, but you could make the same argument for any convention. You should follow in that order:

  1. Your project style guide
  2. Your company style guide
  3. The community style guide

Ideally, the three should be the same.

Update: As of this PR (December 2015), the convention is to always use raise.

Q: Reporting using RStudio A:

Output to Word is tricky. If you haven't already, you might look at the officer and officedown packages as alternatives to quarto. Both start from a template file and insert content based on the styles defined in the template. officer uses functions to add each piece of content. officedown is more like Quarto, in that you define the content using markdown.

https://ardata-fr.github.io/officeverse/office-documents-generation.html

My not-very-experienced impression has been that these produce more reliable output than did my experiments generating Word with Quarto, but it's possible my experience is outdated or that I was doing it wrong.
